investigation.title: Remote Agent Pod Scheduling Failure: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All 6 Nodes
investigation.summary: All three remote-agent checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in the production-api environment because every pod submitted for remote agent creation was rejected by the Kubernetes scheduler with an Unschedulable verdict: 2 of 6 nodes reported Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity and the remaining 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity or selector. No evidence (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) was collected because the agent pod never left the Pending state, so the eval runner could not reach the VM readiness or lifecycle state checks required by the expected-output contract.
investigation.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the production-api remote-agent swarm has exhausted the schedulable kata.peerpods.io/vm resource on the 2 nodes that carry that resource label. The remaining 4 nodes are ineligible due to node affinity or selector mismatch. With 0 of 6 nodes available and preemption unable to free capacity (no preemption victims found), every new remote-agent pod is stuck Unschedulable. This is a cluster-level infrastructure capacity constraint, not an eval runner or source-code defect. No user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence, so impact is scoped to this observability eval.

investigation.title: published-observability-snapshot Eval Fail: Stale Snapshot (snapshotAgeMinutes 323 > max 300)
investigation.summary: The AURA observability eval for `published-observability-snapshot` failed because the published snapshot at https://cypher-asi.github.io/aura-os/observability/status.json was 323 minutes old at eval time, exceeding the contract's maximum allowed age of 300 minutes. This is an isolated eval-layer failure scoped to snapshot freshness; all sibling public-website checks passed, and no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the evidence.
investigation.rootCause: The GitHub Actions workflow responsible for regenerating and publishing the observability snapshot at https://cypher-asi.github.io/aura-os/observability/status.json did not run within the required 300-minute window before the eval executed at 2026-06-30T10:09:09Z. The snapshot was 323 minutes old — 23 minutes past the contract threshold — indicating the upstream workflow was delayed, skipped, or failed to publish a fresh artifact. All other evidence fields in the snapshot (featureCount, hasLiveSource, hasNonUnknownFeatureData, source, generatedAtPresent) passed their assertions, confirming the snapshot content is structurally valid but temporally stale.

possibleCauses: Most likely: The GitHub Actions workflow that publishes the observability snapshot was delayed, skipped, or failed silently, causing the snapshot to go unrefreshed for at least 323 minutes before the eval ran.

Secondary: A GitHub Actions scheduling delay or runner queue backlog caused the workflow to start late, pushing the snapshot age past the 300-minute threshold even if the workflow eventually completed.
Secondary: The workflow ran and completed but failed to commit or push the updated status.json to the GitHub Pages branch, leaving the stale artifact in place.

investigations.title: Remote Agent Pod Scheduling Failure: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All 6 Nodes
investigations.summary: All three remote-agent checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in the production-api environment because every pod submitted for remote agent creation was rejected by the Kubernetes scheduler with an Unschedulable verdict: 2 of 6 nodes reported Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity and the remaining 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity or selector. No evidence (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) was collected because the agent pod never left the Pending state, so the eval runner could not reach the VM readiness or lifecycle state checks required by the expected-output contract.
investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the production-api remote-agent swarm has exhausted the schedulable kata.peerpods.io/vm resource on the 2 nodes that carry that resource label. The remaining 4 nodes are ineligible due to node affinity or selector mismatch. With 0 of 6 nodes available and preemption unable to free capacity (no preemption victims found), every new remote-agent pod is stuck Unschedulable. This is a cluster-level infrastructure capacity constraint, not an eval runner or source-code defect. No user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence, so impact is scoped to this observability eval.

If fetching https://cypher-asi.github.io/aura-os/observability/status.json immediately after the eval shows snapshotAgeMinutes <= 300, the failure was transient (e.g., a CDN propagation delay) rather than a missed workflow run.

If the snapshotAgeMinutes field is computed incorrectly by the runner (e.g., wrong timezone or clock skew in statusSnapshotEvidence), the actual artifact age could be within bounds and the eval would be producing a false positive.
If all subsequent eval runs also fail with snapshotAgeMinutes > 300, the workflow is persistently broken rather than transiently delayed.
